propositions: The test walks 884 renderable units serially, each rendered twice via pandoc (~1768 spawns), costing 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation — exceeding CI's 300s per-test timeout on the macOS lane.
CI's --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread kills the pytest-xdist worker via os._exit(1) from a timer thread, producing worker crashes with no traceback instead of test failures.
The monolithic test loop binds cost to corpus size; corpus growth extends a single test case rather than adding cases, making timeout escape impossible without restructuring.

Chunking the 884 units into fixed-size batches of 40 (parametrized by chunk index) bounds per-test cost to ~4.2s idle, reduces worst case to 38.05s under saturation, and allows xdist to distribute work.
A coverage guard test asserts all chunks reassemble to the full corpus (884 units, >= 100) without weakening the byte-identity property or pandas oracle fidelity.
